spatial_row_ratio: 4:1, 6:1 or 8:1 (4-8 rows of Cotton followed by 1 row of Pigeonpea)
suitable_agro_climatic_zones: Telangana, Vidarbha (Maharashtra), Northern Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh black soil drylands.
agronomic_synergy_and_benefits: Pigeonpea is a deep-rooted legume that accesses subsoil moisture from different soil horizons than cotton. Fixes 40-60 kg atmospheric Nitrogen/ha, improves soil aggregation, and acts as an insurance crop against bollworm crop failure.
economic_land_equivalent_ratio_ler: LER: 1.35 - 1.45 (35-45% greater biological productivity than monocultures)
pest_management_benefit: Pigeonpea serves as a barrier and refuge crop for bollworm parasitoids (Campoletis chloridae and Trichogramma).

spatial_row_ratio: 7:1 or 8:1 (7-8 rows of Groundnut to 1 row of Pigeonpea)
suitable_agro_climatic_zones: Rayalaseema (AP), Southern Telangana (Mahabubnagar), Saurashtra (Gujarat), Karnataka alfisols.
agronomic_synergy_and_benefits: Complementary canopy architecture: Groundnut forms dense horizontal ground cover suppressing weeds and conserving moisture, while Pigeonpea produces tall vertical canopy. Both are legumes contributing biological nitrogen fixation.
pest_management_benefit: Reduces incidence of groundnut leaf miner and tikka leaf spot.

spatial_row_ratio: 4:2 (4 rows of Soybean and 2 rows of Pigeonpea)
suitable_agro_climatic_zones: Madhya Pradesh (Malwa, Nimar, Central Vindhyas), Maharashtra (Vidarbha, Marathwada).
agronomic_synergy_and_benefits: Temporal complementarity: Soybean matures in 90-95 days and is harvested, after which Pigeonpea expands into the vacated space during October-December using residual subsoil moisture.

cropping_system_name: Rice - Chickpea / Bengal Gram Relay Cropping (Paira / Utera)
spatial_row_ratio: Sequential relay broadcasting: Chickpea seeds broadcast into standing paddy 2-3 days before harvest
suitable_agro_climatic_zones: Eastern UP, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal rice fallows.
agronomic_synergy_and_benefits: Utilizes residual soil moisture and capillary water after Kharif rice without tillage; legume root nodules enrich soil nitrogen (30-40 kg N/ha) for succeeding Kharif crops; eliminates fallow land degradation.
pest_management_benefit: Breaks cycle of rice monophagous pests like Yellow Stem Borer and Brown Plant Hopper.

cropping_system_name: Maize + Black Gram / Green Gram Intercropping
suitable_agro_climatic_zones: Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bihar.
agronomic_synergy_and_benefits: Maize utilizes high light and nitrogen, while pulses cover inter-row space rapidly suppressing weeds and fixing 30 kg N/acre. Pulse harvest at 65-70 days provides early cash flow.
pest_management_benefit: Reduces maize stem borer egg laying on primary host.

spatial_row_ratio: 1:2 (2 rows of pulse in 120 cm or 150 cm wide sugarcane inter-row spaces)
suitable_agro_climatic_zones: Western Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Telangana canal command areas.
agronomic_synergy_and_benefits: Sugarcane has slow early formative growth (up to 90 days); short-duration pulses (55-65 days) mature before cane canopy closes, producing 4-6 quintals of pulse grain per acre without reducing cane yields.
pest_management_benefit: Suppresses early weed growth and provides live mulch conserving furrow moisture.

cropping_system_name: Rice - Wheat - Green Gram (Summer Mung) Triple Cropping
spatial_row_ratio: 300% Sequential Cropping Rotation: Kharif Rice -> Rabi Wheat -> Summer Mungbean (60 days)
suitable_agro_climatic_zones: Punjab, Haryana, Western Uttar Pradesh Indo-Gangetic Plains.
agronomic_synergy_and_benefits: Incorporating short-duration summer green gram (SML 668 / Virat) in April-June fixes 40-50 kg N/ha, adds 3 tonnes green biomass/acre upon threshing, and rejuvenates exhausted rice-wheat soil organic carbon.
economic_land_equivalent_ratio_ler: Cropping Intensity: 300%; saves 25% fertilizer N in succeeding paddy
pest_management_benefit: Reduces Phalaris minor seed bank through summer solarization and tillage.

suitable_agro_climatic_zones: Semi-Arid Tropics: Deccan Plateau, Karnataka, Maharashtra drylands.
agronomic_synergy_and_benefits: Proven risk-aversion cropping system for drought-prone drylands; Sorghum harvested at 100 days; Pigeonpea continues to grow until 160 days on deep vertisol moisture.
pest_management_benefit: Minimizes Striga weed emergence and builds predatory insect populations.

agronomic_synergy_and_benefits: Mustard tall stature acts as windbreak; roots explore different soil layers; Chickpea fixes atmospheric nitrogen; mustard acts as trap crop for pod borer predators.
pest_management_benefit: Mustard glucosinolate root exudates suppress soil-borne fungal pathogens.

spatial_row_ratio: Crop rotation: Kharif Cotton -> Summer Green Manure -> Kharif Groundnut -> Rabi Bengal Gram
agronomic_synergy_and_benefits: Breaks monoculture build-up of Pink Bollworm in soil; groundnut fixes nitrogen, lowering fertilizer cost for succeeding cotton by 25%.
pest_management_benefit: Disrupts life cycle of soil-pupating bollworms.

spatial_row_ratio: 1 row of Maize after every 10 rows of Turmeric; or Castor on borders
suitable_agro_climatic_zones: Telangana (Nizamabad, Jagtial), Andhra Pradesh (Duggirala), Tamil Nadu (Erode).
agronomic_synergy_and_benefits: Maize provides partial shade to turmeric during early scorching summer months (May-June) when young sprouts emerge, reducing sunburn; maize cobs harvested at 85 days.
pest_management_benefit: Reduces shoot borer immigration into turmeric canopy.

cropping_system_name: Dhaincha Green Manure - Rice - Rabi Pulse Rotation
spatial_row_ratio: Sequential rotation: Summer Dhaincha (45 days) -> Kharif Rice -> Rabi Urad / Mung
suitable_agro_climatic_zones: Godavari Delta, Krishna Delta, Cauvery Basin, Punjab, Bengal.
agronomic_synergy_and_benefits: Dhaincha incorporated at 45 DAS adds 8-10 tonnes organic biomass and 60-80 kg N/ha in organic form, lowering chemical nitrogen requirement by 25-50% while improving soil microbial diversity.
economic_land_equivalent_ratio_ler: Sustainable Yield Index (SYI) increases from 0.62 to 0.88
pest_management_benefit: Reduces incidence of sheath blight and nematodes.
